data_note: Crime Intelligence findings are republished from detections the pipeline already ran. District crime figures and the anomaly, clustering, forecast and attribution models run on REAL NCRB + Census 2011 data. FIR-level clusters, offender links and vehicles come from the SYNTHETIC schema-shaped FIR record set (see fir_workspace).

findings.headline: Bengaluru Rural records 227 more cases per 100k than its profile accounts for
findings.summary: The model predicts 344.5/100k for Bengaluru Rural from its socio-economic profile; the recorded rate is 571.5/100k. The gap is what the model cannot explain — local factors, or local registration practice.
signals: Recorded rate exceeds the socio-economic model's expectation
Gap computed per district on the latest reported year
Model out-of-bag R² is 0.0355 — weak, so read the gap as a prompt, not a measurement

method.name: RandomForest regression + SHAP attribution
method.detail: Crime rate regressed on socio-economic indicators; the residual is the part the indicators do not account for.
method.caveat: Low model fit (OOB R² 0.0355). Socio-economic indicators do not explain crime well, which is itself the finding. Never read this as a community-level risk factor.

method.detail: Each district's annual cognizable-case total is standardised against its own 2001–2013 series; |z| ≥ 1.8 is reported.
method.caveat: Recorded crime reflects reporting and registration practice as well as offending. A spike can follow a registration drive.

findings.claim_label: Model projection — not an observed fact
findings.headline: Mysuru is trending up by ~288 cases a year
findings.summary: A linear fit over the district's series projects 7,992 cases for 2014 (range 6,886–9,097). This is a projection from past totals, not a measurement of anything that has happened.
signals: Trend fitted across the district's full reported series
R² 0.853 — moderate fit
Confidence interval spans 2,211 cases

method.name: Ordinary least squares trend projection
method.detail: Linear regression of annual totals on year, extended one year.
method.caveat: A projection, not a fact and not a plan. It assumes the past trend continues and takes no account of policing changes.

method.name: K-means clustering on crime-type signature
method.detail: Districts are described by the share of each crime group in their recorded caseload, then grouped so that districts in a group look more like each other than like the rest. k = 4.

quality.reading: Silhouette 0.3102 — the groups overlap considerably. Treat them as a rough grouping for comparison, not as hard categories.

method.caveat: A profile describes recorded caseload composition. It says nothing about the people who live in a district.
